description: Welcome to Team INVINCIBLE! We are AI & ML developers building an intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring System for space missions. Using Python,our dashboard tracks astronaut vitals , detects anomalies, and triggers health alerts. We welcome innovators skilled in Coding, AI, Web Dev, Data Visualization, and UI/UX Design. Let's turn space-health data into a working prototype!
summary:
Project INVINCIBLE presents AEGIS-7, an autonomous, edge-computed space flight medical command center designed to safeguard astronaut health during deep-space missions where communication delays with Earth make real-time telemedicine impossible.

The platform continuously monitors and visualizes multi-astronaut physiological telemetry—including real-time ECG waveforms, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), arterial pressure, and core temperature—alongside life-support environmental metrics such as cabin CO2 levels, suit pressure, and cosmic radiation flux. Utilizing localized statistical anomaly detection (rolling Z-score analysis), AEGIS-7 immediately flags physiological excursions like acute hypoxia, tachycardia, decompression, and solar particle storms, automatically delivering flight-certified emergency countermeasure checklists. It also integrates an interactive Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT) to track neurocognitive fatigue and microgravity adaptation risks.

Operating entirely offline with zero cloud dependency, AEGIS-7 bridges the critical telemetry gap between Earth ground control and deep-space crews, empowering astronauts with autonomous clinical decision support to maximize crew survivability and mission success.
details:
1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

AEGIS-7 (Project INVINCIBLE) is an autonomous, edge-computed space flight medical command center built to monitor astronaut biometrics and provide automated clinical decision support during deep-space exploration.

The system operates via four synchronized modules:

High-Frequency Biotelemetry Streaming: Continuously collects and visualizes vital signs (real-time ECG waveform, heart rate, blood oxygen SpO2, arterial blood pressure, core temperature) alongside life-support environmental parameters (cabin CO2 percentage, suit pressure, ambient and cumulative cosmic radiation flux).

Autonomous Anomaly Detection Engine: Analyzes streaming telemetry buffers using rolling statistical Z-score algorithms to instantly flag dangerous physiological excursions (e.g., acute hypoxia, tachyarrhythmia, hypercapnia, and cabin decompression).

Automated Clinical Checklists: When an excursion is detected, the system immediately presents flight-certified emergency countermeasure protocols (e.g., manual O2 bypass, LiOH scrubber loops, radiation storm bunker evacuation).

Integrated Cognitive & Microgravity Assessment: Features an interactive Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT) measuring millisecond-level reaction times to track neurocognitive fatigue alongside trackers for muscle atrophy, intraocular pressure (IOP), and Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS).

Multi-Crew Tracking: Allows seamless switching between crew members (Commander, Pilot, Medical Specialist) with individualized baseline physiology.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

Zero-Latency Autonomy: Operates 100% locally on spacecraft hardware with zero cloud or ground dependency, overcoming interplanetary communication delays (up to 22 minutes to Mars).

Pre-Symptomatic Warning: Detects early compensatory physiological responses (such as elevated heart rate before severe oxygen desaturation) before irreversible clinical decompensation occurs.

Reduced Cognitive Load in Emergencies: Delivers immediate, unambiguous triage instructions so astronauts can execute countermeasures without panic or procedural hesitation.

Comprehensive Multi-Factor Integration: Correlates astronaut vitals directly with cabin environmental life-support sensors, providing holistic situational awareness.

3. What is the Intended Impact?

Deep Space Exploration (Artemis & Mars): Drastically improves crew survival odds on long-duration lunar and interplanetary missions where ground-directed telemedicine is impossible.

Terrestrial Remote Medicine: The same edge-computed, zero-cloud architecture can be deployed in extreme Earth environments, including Antarctic research stations, submarines, deep mining expeditions, and remote disaster relief zones.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, and Software Used

Languages & Architecture: HTML5, CSS3, modern vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Canvas 2D API for 60 FPS sparkline waveform rendering.

Styling & HUD Design: Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, Google Fonts (Orbitron, Share Tech Mono, Rajdhani).

Audio Synthesis: Web Audio API (custom dual-frequency oscillator and gain envelope synthesis for alarms without external audio files).

Mathematical & ML Algorithms: Rolling 30-second buffer statistics, standard deviation and dynamic Z-score anomaly scoring.

Version Control & Deployment: Git, GitHub, and GitHub Pages for automated static edge hosting with HTTPS enforcement.

5. How is the Project Creative & Unique?

Aerospace HUD Ergonomics: Combines sci-fi aesthetic inspired by modern spaceflight consoles with practical human-factors engineering (scanlines, high-contrast HUD cards, color-coded status beacons) optimized for low-light spacecraft cabins.

Interactive Mission Stress Bench: Includes manual override controls and interactive sliders for physical workload (exercise) and cabin stress, enabling crew to simulate emergencies (Hypoxia, Tachycardia, Solar Flares, CO2 Leaks) for simulation drill training.

Active Cognitive Testing: Unlike passive dashboards, AEGIS-7 actively assesses crew cognitive readiness via an embedded, millisecond-accurate PVT reaction test.

6. Key Factors Considered

Communication Latency: Deep-space signal delays required a solution that never relies on an external server or API to function.

Spaceflight Human Physiology: Incorporates microgravity health hazards such as fluid shifts, bone/muscle deconditioning, high cosmic radiation limits (NASA 600 mSv career limit), and circadian fatigue.

High-Stress Usability: Designed for high readability under sensory overload, using prominent vital gauges, unambiguous color states (Cyan for nominal, Amber for caution, Rose for critical), and immediate audible alerts.
